# Test API parity with darwinkit for CGContextMoveToPoint
# This test compares our generated CGContextMoveToPoint to darwinkit's
#
# GOAL: Generate code that matches or improves upon darwinkit's API
#
# Current darwinkit signature:
#   func CGContextMoveToPoint(c unsafe.Pointer, x unsafe.Pointer, y unsafe.Pointer)
#
# Our goal signature (type-safe):
#   func CGContextMoveToPoint(c CGContextRef, x CGFloat, y CGFloat)
#
# This is an ASPIRATIONAL test - we're already better than darwinkit in some ways
# (type safety), but this test ensures we maintain API compatibility.

env INPUT_DIR=$HOME/.appledocs/cache/developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation

# Generate CoreGraphics bindings with MoveToPoint
exec generate-framework-bindings -framework CoreGraphics -input $INPUT_DIR -filter CGContextMoveToPoint -output cg_test

# Verify the function was generated
exists cg_test/coregraphics/functions.gen.go

# Check that CGContextMoveToPoint exists
grep 'func CGContextMoveToPoint' cg_test/coregraphics/functions.gen.go

# Verify it has the correct typed signature (better than darwinkit's unsafe.Pointer)
grep 'func CGContextMoveToPoint(c CGContextRef, x CGFloat, y CGFloat)' cg_test/coregraphics/functions.gen.go

# Check for the internal variable declaration
grep '_CGContextMoveToPoint func(CGContextRef, CGFloat, CGFloat)' cg_test/coregraphics/functions.gen.go

# Verify types are defined
exists cg_test/coregraphics/types.gen.go
grep 'type CGContextRef' cg_test/coregraphics/types.gen.go
grep 'type CGFloat' cg_test/coregraphics/types.gen.go

# Create a test to compare against darwinkit's actual package
mkdir compare_test
exec sh -c 'cat > compare_test/go.mod <<EOF
module comparetest

go 1.24

require (
	github.com/ebitengine/purego v0.9.0
	github.com/progrium/darwinkit v0.5.0
)
EOF'

# Create a comparison test file
exec sh -c 'cat > compare_test/compare_test.go <<EOF
package comparetest

import (
	"testing"
	"unsafe"

	darwinkit "github.com/progrium/darwinkit/macos/coregraphics"
)

// This test documents the API differences between our generator and darwinkit
func TestAPIParity(t *testing.T) {
	// Darwinkit signature (current):
	// func CGContextMoveToPoint(c unsafe.Pointer, x unsafe.Pointer, y unsafe.Pointer)

	// Our signature (goal):
	// func CGContextMoveToPoint(c CGContextRef, x CGFloat, y CGFloat)

	// Both should be callable, but ours is type-safe

	// Document that darwinkit uses unsafe.Pointer
	var _ func(unsafe.Pointer, unsafe.Pointer, unsafe.Pointer) = darwinkit.CGContextMoveToPoint

	t.Log("Darwinkit uses unsafe.Pointer for all parameters")
	t.Log("Our generator produces type-safe CGContextRef and CGFloat")
	t.Log("This is an improvement in type safety while maintaining C interop")
}
EOF'

# Verify the test compiles (documents the difference)
exec go test -C compare_test -v

# ASPIRATIONAL: Compare full package-level API
# When ready, we could do:
# exec go doc -all ./cg_test/coregraphics > our_api.txt
# exec go doc -all github.com/progrium/darwinkit/macos/coregraphics > darwinkit_api.txt
# exec diff -u darwinkit_api.txt our_api.txt

# SUCCESS CRITERIA:
# 1. CGContextMoveToPoint is generated with type-safe signature
# 2. Function is callable from Go code
# 3. Types (CGContextRef, CGFloat) are properly defined
# 4. API is at least as good as darwinkit (we add type safety)
